- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.75) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next period.
- After a sharp price spike (forecast > 85), model often overshoots; cap forecast at +5% above peak or adjust downward if sentiment turns neutral/negative.
- If sentiment shows strong negative signals (≤0.20) in last 3–5 days, model overcorrects downward; add 1–2% to forecast to avoid premature bottoming.
- Model underestimates prices when sentiment is weak but price is trending upward; increase forecast by 1–3% if sentiment is low but recent price is rising.
- Forecast horizon 30d shows persistent lag: model often misses early price reversals; adjust forecast to align with sentiment shift 1–2 days ahead.
- When sentiment is mixed (0.3–0.7), model tends to average out; use sentiment-weighted moving average to smooth forecast.
- If sentiment is high but price is flat or declining, model overreacts; reduce forecast by 2–4% to reflect sentiment divergence.
- Model often overestimates mean reversion after strong moves; if sentiment is neutral, forecast should be closer to 30-day moving average than to peak.
